page: Amazon Web Services r8a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs (1 thread per core) clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 128 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 6 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8 GB of RAM allocated per core. It provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance includes no local storage and does not feature dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core performance, recording 3773.38 in stress-ng and 2819.0 in Geekbench single-core, alongside a multi-core Geekbench score of 21849.0. Memory throughput reaches 109.04 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 67.91 GB/sec for large-block writes. Data processing metrics are similarly strong, showing 41.51 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 277.76 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. In lightweight machine learning inference, the small 135M model generates 471.96 tokens per second, while general CPU multi-threading and PassMark database operations land in the middle tier.

Hardware tradeoffs include the absence of included ephemeral local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent or temporary file needs. By offering dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores paired with high-bandwidth DDR5 memory, the instance delivers high resource density and consistent throughput. These attributes make the r8a.4xlarge appropriate for memory-heavy enterprise applications, in-memory caches, distributed analytics, and large relational or NoSQL database workloads requiring substantial RAM allocations.

Built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture, it provides 128 GB of DDR5 memory at 6 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Network performance features an 8 Gbps baseline, and the instance operates without local storage or GPUs. Benchmark testing shows top-tier single-core execution with a Geekbench single-core score of 2819.0, accompanied by strong memory throughput achieving 109.04 GB/sec on uncached reads. Workload metrics indicate high efficiency in single-threaded compression and lightweight model token generation, alongside solid multi-core performance. With dense memory allocation and predictable dedicated physical cores, the r8a.4xlarge is well positioned for in-memory databases, memory-intensive analytical processing, and distributed caching layers.
